- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later days.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 80+ levels), then sharply correct downward — model fails to capture this “rebound” or “mean reversion” effect.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher prices, particularly in the 70–75 range, suggesting it underweights downward momentum or overweights short-term volatility.
- Model often lags true price declines — true prices drop faster than forecasted, especially in the 60–65 range.
- Model tends to overreact to recent high prices, producing overly optimistic forecasts when prices are already trending down.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of downward corrections after spikes — true prices fall more sharply than predicted.
- Model shows weak sensitivity to recent low prices — fails to adjust forecasts downward when prices are already near support levels.
- Model exhibits “sticky” behavior — forecasts resist mean reversion, holding high values even when true prices are falling.
